texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 1.2.1997 at about 3.3. p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 9 boards containing packets of lime pickles from the first accused. The second accused is the licencee of the said shop. After taking the sample as per law, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst. The report of the public analyst would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for lime pickle and therefore the same was adulterated. On the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Ext. P16 report of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for lime pickle and hence the same was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts.P1 to P23 series were marked for the prosecution. No evidence was adduced on the side of the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Sections 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act. The report of the analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Sections 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act . A Division Bench of this Court in judgment dated 17-11-2015 in Crl.M.C. No. 417 of 2011 held that the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) is applicable to all Hariprasad vs State Of Kerala (Food Inspector on 8 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198119018/ 2 cases.
